candidates.finding: Could the first-party VFS child merge overwrite an outside newer version when the clean-merge stub accepts a stale child?
candidates.screening_result: Current original elij/macher-agent main@1b8e48d80779a7f54fde71908943d4b773e4bf05 (GPL-3.0) differs from assessed f607863. First-party macher-agent-vfs.el macher-agent--merge-contexts applies child pending curr to parent via macher-agent--update-context-file; another code path macher-agent--sync-context-entry resets staged content on outside modification. A stale-child external-edit overwrite remains plausible but not independently reproduced under supported live Emacs VFS semantics. No source-native RED/GREEN, derivative code, fork or external PR.
candidates.blocker: Current child context merge directly updates parent VFS from pending child entries, but there is no Emacs binary on the authenticated validation host and no first-party matched stale-parent/child native RED replay. Dynamic external-edit synchronization may alter which state is current at merge time. Without a native evidence-supported scenario and target-native test runner, no fix or external PR.

candidates.finding: Could two concurrently supported coding sessions both begin one issue after reading Linear state before either publishes an In Progress claim?
candidates.screening_result: Current original coleam00/Linear-Coding-Agent-Harness main@c37dc096993011cb0cc48a0afab176cd9c8f2375 (MIT) matches Index pin. First-party prompts/coding_prompt.md reads In Progress, prohibits another owner's task, and sets issue In Progress with mcp__linear__update_issue; client.py forwards Linear MCP APIs and does not implement compare-and-swap. A possible two-peer read-then-claim race is an explicitly bounded external integration limitation, not independently demonstrated product-native defect. Original open PR #4 changes SDK integration, no overlap assumed. No patch or native tests.
candidates.blocker: First-party prompt provides only non-atomic Linear issue status conventions, already noted in Index assessment; no first-party deterministic claim transaction, race reproducer, or target-owned CAS capability is shown. Testing live Linear multi-agent conflicts or changing third-party Linear semantics is outside current native no-provider boundary.

candidates.finding: Does dev new retain an unowned or inaccessible created worktree when the agent launch fails after successful provisioning?
candidates.screening_result: Current original basnijholt/agent-cli main@7de04affc3b8bc758a11c75ce555e5097b71b363 (MIT) differs from Index pin. dev new creates a worktree, then applies environment setup/agent launch and displays a dev-environment-created summary. First-party dev list/path/remove make retained worktrees actionable. A failure to start an iTerm2 agent is separately reported in original issue #423, no matched native Linux/macOS failure or automatic-cleanup safety case demonstrated. No new code, RED/GREEN or external PR.
candidates.blocker: First-party dev new intentionally provisions a durable editable worktree before optional agent launch; no native test demonstrates an unowned unsafe orphan instead of the documented recoverable dev environment. Original open issue #423 reports misleading process-launch success specifically for macOS/iTerm2 and requires a macOS native launch proof, unavailable on this Linux host. Any issue-origin fix would be ASSESSMENT_INFORMED, not silently upgraded to derived.

candidates.finding: Can a post-worktree session provisioning failure leave a ghost tracked worktree preventing safe retry without an agent?
candidates.screening_result: Current original agent-of-empires/agent-of-empires main@61058ce97b2813c98674d6d575f6d2dd053c9dbe (MIT) differs materially from 2026-10-27 Index pin. InstancePlan::provision tracks branch/worktree ownership even after partial failure using BuildResult/BuildFailure. Native server/session_spawn.rs converts failure to retained created_worktree and created_workspace_worktrees, and PurgeTransaction::reserve_failed_creation(...).complete_creation_rollback(...) removes only owned worktree/branch on failures including hook/finalization. Current code includes first-party pre_launch_hook_failure_rolls_back_resources_and_owner and post_launch_finalization_failure_rolls_back_without_deadlock tests. No matched source-native leak or needed fix; source inspection only, no new tests.

candidates.finding: Can cancellation between isolated delegate worktree creation and registration leak a lifetime lock without recoverable ownership?
candidates.screening_result: Current original aakshintala/fiber main@297cdb6a1a2740fc82c6e3374c6a5ab359776b8a (MIT), changed from assessed 61af2a8. First-party delegate.rs registers a worktree guard in WorktreeRun before Runner::spawn and on spawn/process_identity errors calls runner.end_worktree; registry.admit owns the start gate. First-party docs/delegates.md explicitly describe retained dirty worktrees and resume lifecycle. No first-party evidence for orphaned lock from cancellation between create and register under supported operation. Owner docs/workflow.md require ticket/owner approval for significant changes, none claimed. Native Rust cargo unavailable on host, no new tests run; no patch.
